newsitem.title: INDIA: India call eases on inflows, poor demand, gilts up.
newsitem.headline: India call eases on inflows, poor demand, gilts up.

text.p: Indian call money eased on lack of demand and improved inflows from interest payments on government securities to end Tuesday at 1.5 percent against the opening 4.0-4.5 percent, dealers said.
They said poor demand for funds pushed rates down as most banks seemed to have covered their positions ahead of the reporting day on Thursday.
"The number of holidays this week seems to have to have prompted many banks to cover their positions in advance," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
Banks are open only for three days in most parts of India this week. They were closed on Monday for a Hindu festival and will be closed on March 28 for Good Friday.
Dealers said interest payments on government securities had also added to the liquidity.
"There have been interest payments on a number of securities with the major one being the 12.50 percent 2004," said a dealer. "I think the total inflows have been around 10 billion rupees."
Dealers said trade in government securities was moderate and volumes fell to 1.67 billion rupees from 2.37 billion on Saturday. Prices moved up in most stocks, they said.
Dealers said buying interest was focused on stocks with maturities up to 2002.

The 13.50 percent 1997 traded on Tuesday at 101.55 rupees against its last traded price of 101.50, the 13.50 percent 1998 improved to 103.25 from 103.20 and the 13.40 percent 1999 to 102.27 from 102.18, dealers said.
Dealers said the treasury bill maturing on October 10 was traded at a yield of 10.05 percent against 10.0 percent.
They said there were no trades in certificates of deposit or commercial paper.
